metadata.title: wav2vec 2.0: A Framework for Self-Supervised Learning of Speech Representations

problem.value: Labeled training data is much scarcer than unlabeled data, making current speech recognition systems difficult to scale for thousands of languages.

evidence.quote: However, in many settings labeled data is much harder to come by than unlabeled data: current speech recognition systems require thousands of hours of transcribed speech to reach acceptable performance which is not available for the vast majority of the nearly 7,000 languages spoken worldwide [31].

contributions.value: We present a framework for self-supervised learning of representations directly from raw audio data.

evidence.quote: In this paper, we present a framework for self-supervised learning of representations from raw audio data.

contributions.value: We learn discrete speech units via a gumbel softmax to represent latent representations in the contrastive task.

evidence.quote: As part of training, we learn discrete speech units [53,32,7,18] via a gumbel softmax [24,5] to represent the latent representations in the contrastive task (Figure 1) which we find to be more effective than non-quantized targets.
This demonstrates the feasibility of speech recognition with limited amounts of labeled data.
We set a new state of the art on TIMIT phoneme recognition as well as the 100 hour clean subset of Librispeech.

method_summary.value: The architecture comprises a multi-layer convolutional feature encoder that converts raw audio into latent representations, a Transformer context network, and a quantization module using product quantization and Gumbel-softmax.

evidence.quote: Our model is composed of a multi-layer convolutional feature encoder f : X → Z which takes as input raw audio X and outputs latent speech representations z 1 , . . . , z T for T time-steps.

method_summary.value: The self-supervised pre-training objective involves masking portions of the feature encoder outputs and solving a contrastive task to identify the true quantized latent speech representation among distractors, combined with a codebook diversity loss.

evidence.quote: During pre-training, we learn representations of speech audio by solving a contrastive task L m which requires to identify the true quantized latent speech representation for a masked time step within a set of distractors.

method_summary.value: Fine-tuning for speech recognition is performed by adding a randomly initialized linear projection on top of the context network and optimizing via CTC loss while keeping the feature encoder frozen.

evidence.quote: Pre-trained models are fine-tuned for speech recognition by adding a randomly initialized linear projection on top of the context network into C classes representing the vocabulary of the task [4].

novelty.value: Unlike prior work such as vq-wav2vec, the model builds context representations over continuous speech representations and uses self-attention to capture dependencies over the entire sequence end-to-end.

evidence.quote: Compared to vq-wav2vec [5], our model builds context representations over continuous speech representations and self-attention captures dependencies over the entire sequence of latent representations end-to-end.

novelty.value: Instead of fixed positional embeddings, the model uses a convolutional layer acting as a relative positional embedding followed by GELU and layer normalization.

evidence.quote: Instead of fixed positional embeddings which encode absolute positional information, we use a convolutional layer similar to [37,4,57] which acts as relative positional embedding.

evidence.quote: First, we tried to improve the continuous input and continuous target model ( § 5.4) by adding an MLP on top of the continuous target representation and we also tried to use a separate set of encoder parameters for the representations used as input and targets (Separate encoders).

ablations.value: Ablating receptive field size, diversity penalty weight, number of relative positional embeddings, gradient flow from quantizer, number of negatives, negative sampling strategy, Gumbel noise, and number of codebooks

evidence.quote: Increasing the receptive field size from 25ms to 30ms had little effect.

future_work.value: Switching to a sequence-to-sequence architecture and word piece vocabulary for performance gains

evidence.quote: We expect performance gains by switching to a seq2seq architecture and a word piece vocabulary.

ethics.value: Making speech recognition technology available to more languages and dialects

evidence.quote: We hope our work will make speech recognition technology more broadly available to many more languages and dialects.

claims.value: Experiments using all labeled data of Librispeech achieve 1.8/3.3 WER on the clean/other test sets.

evidence.quote: Experiments using all labeled data of Librispeech achieve 1.8/3.3 WER on the clean/other test sets.

claims.value: Using just ten minutes of labeled data and pre-training on 53k hours of unlabeled data achieves 4.8/8.2 WER.

evidence.quote: Using just ten minutes of labeled data and pre-training on 53k hours of unlabeled data still achieves 4.8/8.2 WER.

claims.value: Jointly learning discrete speech units with contextualized representations achieves substantially better results than fixed units learned in a prior step.

evidence.quote: Our results show that jointly learning discrete speech units with contextualized representations achieves substantially better results than fixed units learned in a prior step [4].
